'''Gorneesh's tribe''' was a large group of [[Dulok/Legends|Duloks]] from the [[Dulok Swamp]] on the [[Endor/Legends|Forest Moon of Endor]]. Their village was located close to the [[Ewok/Legends|Ewoks]] of [[Bright Tree Village/Legends|Bright Tree Village]], and the two groups had a long history of animosity. Over several encounters, the Duloks attacked the Ewoks' [[Soul Tree]]s, attempted to cut down the [[Tree of Light]], and kidnapped young Ewoks to row a battleship. In other situations, the Duloks found themselves pawns in the schemes of other enemies of the Bright Tree Ewoks, such as [[Morag]] and the [[Stranger]]. Gorneesh's Duloks maintained an uneasy alliance with Morag due to their mutual hatred of the Ewoks.

Prominent members of the tribe included King [[Gorneesh/Legends|Gorneesh]], his wife, [[Urgah]], and his son, [[Boogutt]]. The king was advised by his medicine man, [[Umwak]], and the oracle [[Murgoob]]. He employed several bodyguards, including Duloks that painted symbols on their bellies, such as an [[Unidentified Dulok (X)|X]], an [[Unidentified Dulok (O)|O]], and a [[Unidentified Dulok (diamond)|diamond]].

==Members==
[[Gorneesh/Legends|Gorneesh's]] tribe was a relatively large band of [[Dulok/Legends|Duloks]]<ref name="SWE">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> who lived in the [[Dulok Swamp]] near [[Happy Grove/Legends|Happy Grove]].<ref name="TRGb">''[[The Red Ghost: An Ewok Adventure]]''</ref> The members of the tribe all displayed similar markings: green body fur, brown brows, gray masks around the eyes, and gray lips.<ref name="SWETV">[[Ewoks (television series)|''Ewoks'']].</ref>

By [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], the tribe had come under the rule of King Gorneesh, a hulking, one-eyed Dulok who died his feet red and carried a large [[Club/Legends|club]]. The Dulok frequently led raiding parties against the Ewoks and hatched schemes against them to steal their harvest, kidnap their woklings, and take over their village.<ref name="E10">[[Ewoks (1985) 10|''Ewoks'' (1985) 10]]</ref>

Gorneesh was joined in these endeavors by his tribemates, including his wife, Queen [[Urgah]],<ref name="TTJ">{{Ewoks|The Travelling Jindas}}.</ref> and son, Prince [[Boogutt]].<ref name="Ewoks 1985 13">[[Ewoks (1985) 13|''Ewoks'' (1985) 13]].</ref> Gorneesh was advised by the [[Shaman/Legends|shaman]] [[Umwak]], who also acted as a liaison with [[Morag]]<ref name="TCOTT">{{Ewoks|The Cries of the Trees}}.</ref> and worked with his [[Umwak's nephew|nephew]].<ref name="TTOL">{{Ewoks|The Tree of Light}}.</ref> The oracle [[Murgoob]] was an elder member of the tribe who occasionally offered ideas to help defeat the Ewoks.<ref name="WW">{{Ewoks|Wicket's Wagon}}.</ref> The king frequently surrounded himself with bodyguards, including Duloks marked by an [[Unidentified Dulok (X)|X]], [[Unidentified Dulok (O)|O]], and a [[Unidentified Dulok (diamond)|diamond]] on their fur.<ref name="SWETV" />

==History==
The tribe had a long history of conflict with the [[Ewok/Legends|Ewoks]] of [[Bright Tree Village/Legends|Bright Tree Village]]. Three generations before 3 ABY, the tribes were already embroiled in the [[Ewok–Dulok wars/Legends|Ewok–Dulok wars]]. During one important battle, Duloks from the tribe marched on the Ewoks' [[Soul Tree]]s to cut them down. Their plan was stymied, however, when the Ewok [[Erpham Warrick]] counterattacked in his [[Ewok battle wagon]]. The Duloks retreated to their swamps.<ref name="WW" />

By 3 ABY, Duloks from the tribe often found themselves compelled to do the bidding of other, more powerful enemies of the Ewoks. In one instance, Morag ordered the tribe to keep watch over the [[Phlog/Legends|Phlog]] infant [[Nahkee]], whom she had kidnapped from his family. When a band of young Ewoks freed the child, the enraged Phlog parents rampaged through the Dulok Swamp.<ref name="ROTP">{{Ewoks|Rampage of the Phlogs}}.</ref> In another encounter, an otherworldly being known as the [[Stranger]] compelled the Duloks to raid Bright Tree Village and create a distraction to cover him stealing the Ewoks' [[Sunstar/Legends|Sunstar]].<ref name="NOTS">{{Ewoks|Night of the Stranger}}.</ref> That same year, Gorneesh's tribe stole [[shadowroot soap]] from the Ewoks, invaded their village,<ref name="THV">{{Ewoks|The Haunted Village}}.</ref> helped destroy the [[sun crystal]],<ref name="E13">[[Ewoks (1985) 13|''Ewoks'' (1985) 13]]</ref> and kidnapped young Ewoks to care for the Dulok pups'<ref name="TTJ" /> and clean the Dulok Swamp.<ref name="ROTP" />

Gorneesh's tribe learned that the Ewoks' sacred [[Tree of Light]] had weakened and needed to be renewed. He rushed with a band of his warriors to cut it down before the Ewoks could reach it. The two sides clashed at the site, and the Ewoks [[Wicket Wystri Warrick/Legends|Wicket Wystri Warrick]] and [[Kneesaa a Jari Kintaka/Legends|Kneesaa a Jari Kintaka]] turned the tide against Gorneesh's forces, who were forced to retreat.<ref name="TTOL" />

Eventually, the tribe learned that the Wicket W. Warrick was rebuilding his great-grandfather's battle wagon. On the advice of the Dulok oracle, Murgoob, Gorneesh ordered the battle wagon stolen so that it might be turned against the Ewoks' Soul Trees. Warrick and another Ewok, [[Malani]], foiled the plot when they caused the battle wagon to collapse.<ref name="WW" />

Gorneesh and his warriors later stole a sacred fish carving from their Bright Tree rivals and used it on a Dulok battleship. Nevertheless, some Ewok slaves used to row the vessel escaped and managed to recover the item for the Ewoks.<ref name="PB">{{Ewoks|Prow Beaten}}.</ref>

The Dulok king finally offered to end the war later in 3 ABY, proposing a peace treaty.<ref name="D4">[[Droids (1986) 4|''Droids'' (1986) 4]]</ref> This was but a scheme, however, for as soon as the Ewoks under Chief [[Chirpa/Legends|Chirpa]] reached the site of the [[Chirpa–Gorneesh peace summit|peace summit]], Gorneesh ordered his warriors to cut the bridge the Ewoks were crossing.<ref name="E10" />

Gorneesh's tribe was later [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], with their village destroyed. Only one member of the tribe, [[Agluk]], managed to escape captivity, costing him his right arm in the process. His escape alerted the Ewoks to the Imperial presence on the moon.<ref name="Shadows of Endor">''[[Star Wars: Ewoks—Shadows of Endor]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
King Gorneesh and his tribe first appeared in the [[Ewoks (television series)|''Ewoks'']] animated series, which began airing in 1985. They feature in 8 of the 13 episodes of the first season and 3 of the 35 of the second.<ref name="SWETV" /> Critics and ''Star Wars'' authors have singled out some of these episodes as examples of the series at its best. [[Jon Bradley Snyder]], for instance, has identified "[[Asha (episode)|Asha]]" as a first-season highlight, "[[Wicket's Wagon]]" as well animated, and "[[Rampage of the Phlogs]]" as one of the more humorous episodes thanks to the scene in which King Gorneesh has to change the diaper of a baby Phlog.<ref name="SWCEL">{{InsiderCite|27|A Star Wars CELibration|A ''Star Wars'' CELibration}}</ref> [[Daniel Wallace|Dan Wallace]] and [[Robin Pronovost]] have named the episodes "[[The Tree of Light]]," "[[Wicket's Wagon]]," and "Asha" as those that best show the villainy of Gorneesh and his tribemates.<ref name="COE 4">{{Hyperspace|url=fans/hyperspace/source/feature20081201.html|text=Castaways of Endor|int=Castaways of Endor}}</ref>

A variety of tie-in items were released during the run of ''Star Wars: Ewoks,'' including Dulok action figures from [[Kenner Products|Kenner]]<ref name="toy">[[Star Wars: Ewoks (toy line)|''Star Wars: Ewoks'' toy line]].</ref><ref name="Star Wars: The Action Figure Archive">''[[Star Wars: The Action Figure Archive]]''</ref> and storybook adaptations. Three Dulok-themed books were released: ''[[The Red Ghost: An Ewok Adventure]]'' from [[Random House]] in 1986 (based on the episode "Asha"), and [[The Haunted Village (book)|''The Haunted Village'']] and [[Wicket's Wagon (book)|''Wicket's Wagon'']] from [[Dragon Picture Books]] in 1987, based on the episodes of the same name. While ''The Red Ghost'' includes all-new artwork, the Dragon volumes use images taken directly from the cartoons. The Dragon volumes misspell the species' name ''Dulock''. In [[1986]], Dulok characters took to the ice as part of "[[The Ewoks and the Magic Sunberries]]."<ref name="AGP blog 35">{{Blog|abelgpena|35|Ewoks at the Ice Capades}}.</ref> Lucasfilm repackaged several episodes of the animated series as the feature-length films [[The Haunted Village (film)|''The Haunted Village'']] and ''[[Tales from the Endor Woods]]'' in [[2004]]. Works that mention Duloks published in the years since the series' cancellation, such as ''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe]]'', the ''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', and the various [[Star Wars: Essential Guides|''Essential Guides'']], simply summarize events from the television series.
